front: What ancient wonder was a lighthouse on the island of Pharos in Egypt?
back: Lighthouse of Alexandria — one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, built around 280 BC, stood approximately 100 meters tall

front: Which Italian landmark is famous for its unintended tilt?
back: Leaning Tower of Pisa — bell tower begun in 1173, tilts due to soft foundation soil, currently leans at about 4 degrees

front: What is the largest ancient amphitheater ever built?
back: The Colosseum in Rome — completed in 80 AD, could hold 50,000-80,000 spectators for gladiatorial contests

front: Which Indian monument was built by Shah Jahan as a mausoleum for his wife?
back: Taj Mahal — white marble mausoleum in Agra, completed around 1653, considered a masterpiece of Mughal architecture

front: What is the world's tallest building as of 2024?
back: Burj Khalifa in Dubai — stands at 828 meters (2,717 feet), completed in 2010, has 163 floors

front: Which ancient Greek temple on the Acropolis was dedicated to Athena?
back: The Parthenon — built between 447-432 BC in Athens, considered the finest example of Doric architecture

front: What famous structure connects the boroughs of Manhattan and Brooklyn?
back: Brooklyn Bridge — completed in 1883, first steel-wire suspension bridge, designed by John Augustus Roebling

front: Which Spanish architect designed the unfinished Sagrada Família basilica?
back: Antoni Gaudí — construction began in 1882 in Barcelona, combines Gothic and Art Nouveau forms

front: What is the largest Gothic cathedral in the world?
back: Seville Cathedral in Spain — completed in the 16th century, built on the site of a former mosque

front: Which Australian landmark has a distinctive sail-shaped design?
back: Sydney Opera House — designed by Jørn Utzon, opened in 1973, UNESCO World Heritage Site

front: What ancient Mesopotamian temple form resembles a stepped pyramid?
back: Ziggurat — massive terraced structures built in ancient Mesopotamia, served as temples to local gods

front: Which French palace was the principal royal residence from 1682 to 1789?
back: Palace of Versailles — originally a hunting lodge, expanded by Louis XIV into an opulent palace complex

front: What is the longest wall ever built by humans?
back: Great Wall of China — over 21,000 km including all branches, built over many centuries starting in 7th century BC

front: Which New York City skyscraper was the world's tallest for nearly 40 years?
back: Empire State Building — completed in 1931, stood at 381 meters, held record until 1970

front: What ancient stone monument in England consists of a ring of standing stones?
back: Stonehenge — prehistoric monument built in stages from around 3000-2000 BC, purpose remains debated

front: Which tower was built as the entrance arch for the 1889 World's Fair?
back: Eiffel Tower in Paris — designed by Gustave Eiffel, originally 300 meters tall, was meant to be temporary

front: What is the largest religious monument in the world?
back: Angkor Wat in Cambodia — Hindu-Buddhist temple complex built in 12th century, covers 162.6 hectares

front: Which San Francisco landmark is painted 'International Orange'?
back: Golden Gate Bridge — suspension bridge completed in 1937, spans 2,737 meters total

front: What ancient wonder was a massive tomb for Egyptian pharaoh Khufu?
back: Great Pyramid of Giza — built around 2560 BC, oldest of the Seven Wonders and only one still standing

front: Which building in Bilbao revitalized the city and pioneered 'starchitecture'?
back: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao — designed by Frank Gehry, opened 1997, known for titanium curves

front: What Russian landmark features colorful onion domes?
back: Saint Basil's Cathedral in Moscow — built 1555-1561 by Ivan the Terrible, has nine chapels

front: Which ancient Jordanian city was carved into rose-red cliffs?
back: Petra — ancient Nabataean city established around 312 BC, famous for its rock-cut architecture

front: What is the largest dome built before the 20th century?
back: Dome of the Pantheon in Rome — 43.3 meters diameter, built around 125 AD, unreinforced concrete

front: Which London landmark contains the Houses of Parliament?
back: Palace of Westminster — Gothic Revival building rebuilt after 1834 fire, includes Big Ben tower

front: What medieval fortress in Prague overlooks the Vltava River?
back: Prague Castle — largest ancient castle complex in the world at about 70,000 square meters

front: Which Chicago skyscraper pioneered the steel-frame construction method?
back: Home Insurance Building — built 1885, demolished 1931, considered first true skyscraper at 10 stories

front: What ancient Greek outdoor theater had exceptional acoustics?
back: Theater of Epidaurus — built in 4th century BC, seats 14,000, whispers audible from the stage

front: Which Beijing landmark was the Chinese imperial palace for 500 years?
back: Forbidden City — built 1406-1420, has 980 buildings, largest palace complex in the world

front: What German castle inspired Disney's Sleeping Beauty Castle?
back: Neuschwanstein Castle — built for Ludwig II of Bavaria starting 1869, Romanesque Revival style

front: Which ancient Incan citadel sits high in the Peruvian Andes?
back: Machu Picchu — built around 1450 AD at 2,430 meters elevation, rediscovered in 1911
